scenes.heading: Congruent triangles
scenes.sub: Proving two triangles are exact copies
scenes.say: How can you be sure two triangles are exact copies without measuring everything? In this video you will use four congruence tests, write short proofs, and use congruence to find missing sides and angles.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Two cookies from the same cutter match exactly, even if one is flipped
scenes.science: Congruent triangles: same sides and angles, possibly turned or flipped
scenes.breaks: Real cookies spread in the oven; congruent triangles match perfectly.
scenes.say: Press the same cookie cutter into dough twice. One cookie might be turned or flipped, but lay it on the other and they match exactly. Congruent triangles are like that. Real cookies spread a little in the oven, but congruent triangles match perfectly.

scenes.heading: The four tests
points: SAS: two sides and the angle between
AAS: two angles and a matching side
AAA and SSA are NOT tests
scenes.say: Here are the four tests. S S S: three pairs of equal sides. S A S: two sides and the angle between them. A A S: two angles and a side in a matching position. R H S: a right angle, the hypotenuse and one other side. Three equal angles, or two sides with an angle that is not between them, are not enough.

scenes.heading: SAS: the angle is the sandwich filling
scenes.say: First the two triangles, then the markings. Each has sides of six and eight centimetres, and the fifty degree angle sits right between those two sides, like the filling in a sandwich. So the triangles are congruent by S A S, even though one is flipped.
scenes.caption: Each has sides of 6 cm and 8 cm, and the 50° angle sits between them, like the filling in a sandwich. So the triangles are congruent by SAS, even though one is flipped.

scenes.heading: A proof with a parallelogram
notes: Alternate angles: one arc, two arcs
scenes.say: Now a parallelogram with its diagonal. The parallel sides give two pairs of alternate angles, shown with one arc and two arcs. The diagonal is shared by both triangles. Two angles and a side: the triangles are congruent by A A S, which proves that opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: △ABC ≅ △PQR, ∠A = 70°, ∠C = 46°, AB = 10 cm. Find PQ and ∠Q.
lines: PQ matches AB, so PQ = 10 cm
scenes.say: Triangle A B C is congruent to triangle P Q R. P Q matches A B, so it is ten centimetres. Angle Q matches angle B, which is one eighty minus seventy minus forty-six: sixty-four degrees.
scenes.caption: PQ matches AB, so PQ = 10 cm. ∠Q matches ∠B = 180° − 70° − 46° = 64°.

points: ≅ means same shape and same size
scenes.say: Quick recap. Congruent means the same shape and the same size. Write the vertices in matching order. The tests are S S S, S A S, A A S and R H S. And a proof lists the facts with reasons, names the test, then states the congruence. Now try the practice questions!
